name: 逆鳞
look: a long straight sword of archaic make, its dark steel blade forged with overlapping ripples like the scales of a dragon; set into the spine just above a plain, wide cross guard is one real dragon scale the size of a palm, deep slate-green with a bronze rim, taken from its owner's own back; the grip is wrapped in old brown leather rubbed glossy by long use. The inset scale holds a steady inner light like an ember under green glass, and thin threads of that light run a short way up the scale-ripples of the blade. Upright and unbent, stern and simple.

name: 不问来处
look: a short hunting bow of plain pale ash wood, completely bare: no carving, no inlay, no paint, the limbs worn satin-smooth by two hundred years of road travel and darkened only where the hand rests; the bowstring is ordinary twisted animal sinew, clearly newer and lighter in colour than the old wood, and the nocks show the grooves of many earlier strings. The one touch of magic: the worn grip has a soft honey-gold warmth that glows faintly from inside the wood, humble and steady.

name: 长眠不渡
look: an extremely long spear, far taller than a person, its shaft of dense pale wood ground down layer after layer until it is thin as a reed and almost too slender to hold; the whole shaft is covered from end to end with countless tiny carved tally notches, most worn nearly smooth, only the last few still crisp; the leaf-shaped spearhead is rusted to the brown colour of earth, crusted with old soil from standing planted in the ground for centuries. Inside the last notches a very faint pale light swells and fades slowly, like a sleeping creature's breath.

name: 幼铃
look: a thick, heavy two-handed greatsword of dark grey steel, broad and blunt-tipped, with a squared iron cross guard; near the middle of one edge a deep crescent gouge bites into the blade, its rim scored with jagged tooth marks, as if a dragon's jaws had clamped on and the sword was wrenched free; tied to the pommel by a shriveled leather thong hangs a small dry, dull old bronze bell, the kind once hung on a young drake's neck. The little bell carries a faint, warm glint, as though it has just stopped ringing.

name: 空山问
look: a small jaw harp carved from a single piece of ivory-white dragon bone, about the length of a finger, the horseshoe frame smooth and slightly yellowed; one edge of the frame is worn into clear notches by teeth, keeping the shape of the bite of the woman who played it for four hundred years; along both arms of the frame runs a row of tiny uneven graduation marks, bitten into the bone rather than cut. The thin bone tongue in the middle shimmers faintly with pale light, as if still trembling with a note.

name: 半拍长歌
look: a one-handed long sword forged from adamantine, a pale bronze-gold metal with a soft inner sheen; plain soldier's work: a simple straight cross guard, a grip wrapped in faded grey-blue cloth darkened by wall mud, and a scuffed round pommel; the edges carry many small old nicks from sixty years of holding a broken wall; along the spine, from guard to tip, runs a neat row of forty-seven small round dents tapped in one by one with a knuckle. Each dent glows a faint warm gold, like a line of notes in a marching song.

name: 盐里的信
look: a short sword whose blade is ground from a cold, water-coloured bone found in a southern dead land, pale translucent blue-grey, ground for a long time and still not quite straight, with a gentle wavering edge; the whole blade is crusted with a bloom of white salt crystals like hoarfrost, seeping out from inside the bone; the hilt is wrapped in dark, weathered cloth with a plain bone pommel. The salt crystals glitter with a faint, cold white light, and a thin ring of salt has formed around the base of the blade.

name: 衔土阔刀
look: a long single-edged broad blade with a thick heavy back, forged of adamantine (pale bronze-gold metal with an inner sheen); halfway along the edge is one deep, ugly notch, packed full of earth that has compressed over the years into stone, a notch only chopping into the ground could make; the tip is dulled and scratched from being driven into soil; the long grip is bound in rough hemp cord blackened by charcoal soot. Deep inside the earth-packed notch a faint amber glow smolders like a buried ember, as if the line on the ground is still being held.

name: 空环长剑
look: a straight long sword of plain bright steel, workmanlike and well kept; a thin line of pale cyan aether crystal is inlaid along the length of the spine; the grip is wrapped twice in old linen cloth bound in an odd way, leaving one extra small loop of cloth standing out from the grip, just large enough for another person's finger to hook through; the loop is empty and the cloth is stiff and darkened with years of sweat, fused to the grip. The crystal line glows a cool, quiet cyan along the spine.

name: 谷口之鳞
look: a slender long sword of mythic antiquity, its whole blade the colour of clear spring water, a translucent pale aqua like ice over a stream; a single fine crack runs up the spine from the base and stops halfway; set into the round cross guard is one large iridescent scale, silver-blue with a fish-like sheen, that could be from a dragon or from a giant fish; the grip is wrapped in plain undyed hide. Faint light ripples slowly through the blade like sunlight moving through running water.

name: 勾环短剑
look: a short sword of the most ordinary steel, shown half-drawn from its plain brown leather scabbard; a cheap, light blade any smith could make, without a single chip or rust spot, yet dull all over, evenly blunted as if its sharpness had been slowly drained away year by year; the grip is plain cord. On the side of the scabbard one small patch is rubbed bright and glossy, worn by a right index finger hooking a ring for nineteen years. That rubbed spot holds a faint warm gleam, the only thing about it that shines.

name: 未磨白骨
look: a long sword carved from a single piece of bone, pure chalk-white from tip to guard, never sharpened and never polished: the edges are rounded and blunt, the surface keeps the natural porous grain of dragon bone; the hilt, by contrast, is coated with a thick, dark amber patina rubbed glossy by a lifetime of being held but never swung; a simple bone cross guard. Deep inside the white bone a very faint golden glint stirs, the barest shape of spread wings, visible only at certain angles.

name: 奶奶的银剑
look: a slender, narrow silver sword, razor sharp and unnaturally clean, mirror-bright from guard to point with not a single stain; a few clear droplets slide down the blade and fall away without leaving any trace; a delicate silver cross guard and a grip of dark wrapped leather; at the very end of the pommel there is a small shallow dent, pressed in by a thumb over many years, set low and small, the size of a child's thumb. The silver blade has a faint, cool, faultless gleam.

name: 断岭的冢
look: a two-handed adamantine greatsword (pale bronze-gold metal with inner sheen), the blade extremely wide, the edge ground roughly and hastily as if made for immediate use; set into the cross guard is one grey-blue wyvern scale with soft rounded edges, shed naturally from a living beast rather than torn from a corpse; the lower third of the blade toward the tip is stained with a crust of earthy rust that will never wash off; the long grip is wrapped in weathered leather. The rounded scale glows with a warm, quiet light, like a companion still keeping watch.

name: 灰背的牙
look: a two-handed sword ground from one entire enormous dragon tooth, ash-white with streaks of old grey, so the blade curves in a natural arc that no grinding could straighten; the root end of the tooth is left untouched as the hilt, rough and craggy, with one worn smooth ring around it where something rubbed against it for years, partly bound in strips of old leather. Deep inside the tooth a faint glow like a campfire's embers moves slowly, warm orange beneath the pale enamel, a fire that must never go out.

name: 当铺重剑
look: a bare two-handed heavy sword with no scabbard, plain grey steel without any pattern or ornament, a simple bar cross guard, faintly dusty from forty years lying on a pawnshop shelf; one section of the grip is clad in a sheet of copper nailed on by an amateur to keep it from falling apart, the copper slightly crooked and the nail heads uneven. Despite the dust, a thin, clean bright line runs along the whole edge: it is still keen, as if waiting to walk the road again.

name: 蕊珂舞剑
look: an elegant two-handed dancing greatsword, longer and slimmer than a war sword, made for display at a royal feast: a sweeping swept-wing guard and a long hilt weighted with poured lead in a rounded pommel; flecks of worn gilt plating still cling to the guard and blade, but most has rubbed away, showing the plain ordinary steel beneath; a short tassel of faded deep blue silk hangs from the pommel. The one surprise: its edge is truly sharpened, a thin razor line of cold silver light running down both sides.

name: 灰蛾长杖
look: a tall adamantine staff, longer than a person is tall, completely plain without any pattern; its upper end is scorched bone-white by fire, so white that its original bronze-gold colour cannot be seen there, fading down into the pale bronze-gold metal below; low on the shaft is one hand-sized ring of worn depression where it was gripped in exactly the same place for years. A few tiny flakes of grey ash shaped like moths cling to the white tip and lift just off it, glowing faintly at their edges.

name: 钉海之矛
look: a long primeval spear of unknown material: it looks like weathered grey-white stone but has the fine fibrous grain of bone, utterly clean though it lay in the sea for ten thousand years, with no barnacles or weed; a simple, ancient leaf-shaped head; near the tip is a chipped bite, and embedded in the chip is a hard layer of dark, iridescent shell, plainly not part of the spear itself. A slow, deep sea-blue light breathes within the spear's grain like a far-off tide.

name: 过手铁槊
look: a heavy long lance with a long, slightly mismatched wooden shaft, clearly a later replacement; the long tapering blade is made of a cold, water-coloured bone from a southern dead land, translucent pale blue-grey; a pad of folded cloth is tied around the grip because the shaft is too cold to hold bare; where blade meets shaft the iron collar is cut with a column of horizontal tally bars, some deep and some shallow, the lowest ones worn away. A thin rime of frost and a faint cold blue light cling to the bone blade.

name: 岑瓦长戟
look: a tall elegant halberd of long-lived, ageless craft: a crescent axe blade, a slim spike and a back hook of silvery steel; a thin vein of pale cyan aether crystal is set along the shaft; the dark wood shaft is carved from top to bottom with dense rows of small horizontal lines, each with a few tiny scratched marks beside it, crowded like a diary; eleven of the lines are cut deeper and scattered in different places. The aether vein glows with a light, cold cyan, like breath on a winter morning.

name: 锁与半句
look: a staff of true silver a little over three feet long, made of a dozen or so cylindrical segments nested together, each ring able to rotate; the segments are engraved with flowing interlocking patterns that do not quite line up, broken off mid-curve where one ring meets the next; there is no keyhole and no visible seam anywhere, the ends capped smooth. Faint blue-white light runs through the engraved channels but stops at each misaligned joint, waiting for the rings to be turned into place.

name: 长夜一灯
look: a small hand lamp with a brass-copper body, its shell battered and dented all over, the handle ring worn smooth; in place of a wick it holds a finger-length shard of pale cyan aether crystal, one end ground slightly flat by a thumb pressing on it night after night; a short glass chimney with a hairline crack. The crystal burns with a soft, steady pale cyan light that stays inside the lamp, the kind of light you can tell stories by until dawn.

name: 出城的匣
look: a flat square box about a foot on each side, made of adamantine (pale bronze-gold metal with an inner sheen), every corner and edge worn round by travel; the clasp has broken three times and is now twisted shut with a loop of rusty iron wire that was never repaired; the lid is slightly ajar, and the yellowed edges of a layer of old paper show at the bottom, stuck fast to the box. A faint warm light glows out from the narrow gap under the lid, like a candle kept inside.

name: 嘶哑之杯
look: a plain adamantine drinking cup, not very well made: it is pieced together from several pooled scraps of metal, each segment a slightly different shade of bronze-gold, the seams uneven and misaligned; the rim is missing one small chunk, and the broken-off piece hangs beside the cup on a short leather cord, kept but never rejoined. Inside the cup a warm, low golden glow rises like the light of a campfire people gather around.

name: 骨磨之镜
look: a small hand mirror with ragged, irregular edges, ground out of one piece of an enormous ancient bone until its face became polished enough to reflect; the front is a smooth, pale, softly reflective surface like ivory turned to glass; the back is left raw, the original rough bone with an old crack running across it, the crack filled with fine golden sand. The mirror face holds a faint pale-gold shimmer, as if something far away is glancing into it.

name: 折羽之冠
look: a tiny circlet crown, much too small for an adult head, ground from a pair of broken wing bones: thin, white, almost translucent, its band carved with the fine grain of feather vanes; on its rim are two clean, sharp break faces where the wings were snapped off in one stroke; on the inner surface a shallow worn engraved line is barely visible. The white bone gives off a soft pearly glow, gentle and pure, the last trace of a lost divinity.

name: 弑主长弓
look: a tall longbow whose limbs are one continuous piece of pale blue-white bone from an ancient fallen being, dense and heavy like iron, with old ritual notches near the grip from generations who never dared to use it; the bowstring is twisted from long black human hair and is still drawn taut; the grip is bound in dark, worn leather. A cold, quiet sorrow hangs on it; a thin crack of faint pale light runs along the upper limb, like the trace of one arrow loosed.

name: 引路火矢
look: a long bow of true silver, slender and bright; one section of the upper limb is melted and blackened, the silver bubbled and flowed where fire-arrow oil burned on it for three days and nights; the string is a newer replacement; the grip's cloth wrapping is bitten clean through by a ring of deep tooth marks. Within the melted section a small ember-orange glow still pulses slowly, one flash at a time, like a signal fire guiding someone home.

name: 松林之赠
look: a long elegant war bow of dark wood, its limbs lined with thin, perfectly flattened scales that shine the colour of clear water when the light passes over them; the bow is unstrung: its string has been taken off at both ends and wound into a small, very neat coil, tied to the grip with a short cord; a tiny sprig of pine needles is tucked into the grip wrapping. The water-coloured scales ripple with a faint, calm light.

name: 父亲的弓
look: a long bow of pale white wood from the mountains, plain and sturdy; set into the upper limb is a single round gem, clear amber-gold, an heirloom of a chieftain's family never meant for war; the grip is wrapped in two layers: an older smooth leather wrap beneath, and over it a newer, rougher, clumsier wrap of cord added later to fit a smaller hand. The gem catches a single bright star of reflected light, like a signal flashing on a distant ridge.

name: 黎明前的格雷莱恩
look: an absurdly oversized straight single-edged greatsword, its blade like a whole black stone slab chiseled out of a fortress wall: obsidian-black, unsharpened, blunt-edged and immensely heavy; sealed deep inside the obsidian core is a layer of red that never faded after the fire, slowly shifting like molten embers trapped under black glass; the long hilt has no wrapping at all, only bare metal worn deep with grip marks in several places that do not belong to the same hand. Something of three dead divinities lingers in it: silent, enormous, not of this world.

name: 奥古斯都的猎期
look: a colossal dark-gold lance of an ancient magitech empire, the whole shaft crawling with magic circles and runes so dense they become a texture; behind the long tip flares a ring of precisely angled barbs in the dragon-hunting style, made to lock into the gap between scales; every barb is spotless, without a single scratch, for it never met its prey. Its runes glow faintly and drift slowly along the shaft by themselves, perfectly calculated, quietly waiting for a day that never came.

name: 黑曜之名
look: a palm-sized shard of black obsidian, glassy and deep, with sharp conchoidal broken edges on every side as if snapped from something larger; across its face runs one single shallow engraved line of tiny worn carved marks, so faint it can only be seen where light grazes the surface at a slant. Deep within the black glass a faint starry glimmer drifts, as though the darkness inside is much deeper than the stone is thick.

name: 初生白枝
look: a short length of a fresh young branch, pure white bark smooth as porcelain, with one tiny unfurling bud near the top; the cut end is freshly cut and still seeping a single clear bead of sap; it never dries and never darkens. Under the white bark, fine veins of soft pale gold light flow slowly toward the cut, like streams running into a river, and the whole twig gives a gentle impression of warmth.

name: 凝滞之羽
look: a single long white feather, perfectly straight, its central shaft without a single break or bend; every barb lies absolutely still and precise, as though frozen in a moment of time; the white has a faint silvery depth like still deep water. Around its edges space itself seems to hold its breath: a very slight, clear refraction clings to the vane like glass, making it look at once impossibly heavy and weightless.

name: 千风之种
look: a single tiny seed, pale cream and almond shaped, its skin covered with very fine, intricate veins like the map of a wind-swept plain; the vein pattern is subtly mid-shift, as if the lines are slowly flowing in a different direction each time you look; two or three almost invisible threads of pale green-white breeze curl close around it. It neither sprouts nor withers, and it looks so weightless it might drift away.

name: 岚切
look: a long single-edged blade, extremely thin, the steel so fine it is almost translucent, a pale silver tinged with soft green like highland grass under wind; its edge seems to blur, as though the wind arrives a heartbeat before the blade; a simple guard and a long grip bound in pale weathered cord; beside it, a plain scabbard frayed and scoured by wind. Fine curling threads of pale wind trace along the edge and stay close to the steel, swift and quiet.

name: 霜灯
look: a sturdy lantern on a black wrought-iron frame with a ring for hanging, its panes made of mica sheets worn rough and frosted until they look like thin ice; inside there is no oil and no wick, only a single small point of pure white flame that has never been refilled; frost crystals have gathered on the iron corners. The white fire glows steadily through the frosted mica, cold and clear, the light of a beacon at a snowy pass.

name: 铃尾的鼎
look: a small round marching cookpot of hammered copper, sized for halflings, with a hanging bail handle and a hook for the side of a wagon; its bottom has been patched seven times, each riveted patch a darker shade of copper than the one before; the outside is soot-blackened at the base and polished bright at the rim by four generations of use. A soft, warm golden light glows from inside, and a thin curl of steam rises just above the rim, smelling of a meal that will always be enough.

name: 静铃
look: a pair of old, soft running boots of supple brown leather made for the beast-eared folk, scuffed and creased from countless miles, soles worn thin; around each boot's upper is sewn a ring of small brass bells, every clapper removed, so all the bells are silent. Faint silvery light gathers on the mute bells and runs along the soles like a trail of quick wind, swift and soundless.

name: 四路刀
look: a very short knife, little longer than a hand, with a plain flat iron guard; the blade is ground so thin it lets light through at the edge; the grip is wrapped in fresh undyed cloth over layers of older faded wraps, changed many times over two hundred years; the tang end has two old nail holes where it once hung on a doorframe. The thin blade glows faintly with the pale light of dawn, as stubborn as someone who simply will not step aside.

name: 灰炉手
look: a pair of thick cowhide miner's gloves, heavy, cracked and stained dark with coal dust and earth; the right palm wore through completely and was patched with leather cut from another glove, a different, lighter brown, stitched with coarse thread; the fingertips are scuffed raw from digging. A faint ember-like warmth glows inside the patched palm, as if it could keep digging for one more.

name: 白鹿披
look: an old indigo-blue cloak, spread as if hanging, the hem once torn by thorns and mended with very fine, neat little patches in a scholar's tidy stitching; one side of the cloak is scorched brown and stiff at the edge; the collar closes with a small pewter clasp shaped like a white deer's head. The wool holds a faint dewy sheen, tiny beads of water clinging to it that no fire can dry.

name: 冬烬
look: a long fur cloak that would hang to the calf, its outside grey-white fur from the back of a frost-fanged beast lord, its lining a short, dense chestnut-red velvet pile, shown with one side turned open; the collar fastens with a single beast fang worn round and smooth; snowflakes on the shoulder melt into fine beads of water, while the hem stays dry. Scattered in the red velvet are a few tiny glowing red sparks, like embers left under ash after the fire dies.

name: 焚原断刃
look: a broken sword: only about two feet of blade remain, its whole surface a deep dark red like cooled forge iron, the break jagged and uneven; scorch marks streak the steel; the hilt has a simple broad guard, and one side of the grip is worn flat where a thumb pressed against it. Faint dark-red fire smolders deep in the steel and seeps toward the jagged break, the heat of a dragon's death still not cooled.

name: 落日弓
look: a tall longbow about six feet long, made from a fallen forest tree, its wood a deep sombre brown with long grain; the grip is deeply pressed in with the clear shape of five fingers of a right hand, a handprint worn into the wood by one day-long draw; the string is a newer replacement of pale sinew. A warm sunset gold-red glow lingers along the inner face of the limbs, as if the bow still remembers being held fully drawn from dawn to dusk.

name: 无赦之牌
look: thirteen small copper tags strung on a worn leather cord, each about two fingers wide, edges rounded smooth; twelve of them are engraved with simple images, a wolf's head, a flame, water ripples, a stone gate and others, cut by a smith's careful hand; the thirteenth tag is blank and dark. A deep dark-red light shines out from within the engraved lines of the twelve, while the blank last one stays dull.

name: 驯雷的缰
look: a long rein of thick coarse hemp rope, braided without a single knot or joint from end to end, coiled into a heavy loop that could be slung over a shoulder, one end trailing free; the rope is a weathered straw colour, damp and still grippable; one stretch that was held most often is fuzzed with fine white hemp fibres. Those white fibres stand on end with tiny crackling blue-white sparks of lightning dancing between them.

name: 那口锅
look: a big round iron cooking pot about three feet across, thick-walled and blackened by years of campfires on the road, with an arched iron bail handle whose two ends are rubbed shiny; on the bottom there is one dented-in hollow whose rim looks like a ring of tooth marks; the inside is clean and well oiled. A thin wisp of warm white steam curls just above the rim, and a faint glow of heat gathers in the dented spot as though it always bubbles first.

name: 潮与归帆
look: a palm-sized white seashell brooch, its fluted ridge flaring out like a billowing sail on a small ship, the shell surface lustrous and faintly iridescent; a blue-silver clasp pin is fixed to the back; a fine crack runs across the shell, filled and glistening with a line of seawater as if just pulled from the sea, with tiny salt crystals drying along it in the shape of a sail. It seems to hum softly with the sound of a distant tide.

name: 垂天七翼
look: a flying harness of buckled leather straps for shoulders and waist, carrying on its back seven thin wing slats of silver bone, long and curved, overlapping and half fanned open like a narrow shield spreading into wings; there is no cloth between them; the lowest slat has a noticeable bend that has been straightened and has bent back again; at the chest strap a sealed casing holds an old blue-white wind core. Pale blue-white wind shimmers faintly in the gaps between the slats.

name: 霜棘王骸
look: a tall spear like a length of white dragon spine: the head is ground from a single semi-transparent ancient dragon scale, frosted white-blue, gripped at its root by four backward-curving bone spines; the shaft is a frost-white pale wood, with a grip wrapped in thick deep-blue leather. Between the four spines hang tiny glittering needles of ice like little bells, and a thin breath of cold mist clings close to the scale-blade.

name: 莫菈的骨铃
look: a tiny bell carved from pale yellow bone, only as long as a thumb, polished smooth and glossy by generations of hands, with one small chip missing from its rim; its clapper is a single round bone bead that never makes a sound; it hangs from a short loop of faded blue cord. A soft milky-white light glows through the thin bone shell, rising and falling slowly like a calm breath.

name: 群山合扉
look: a massive tower shield tall enough to reach a man's shoulder, cast of adamantine (pale bronze-gold metal with inner sheen), its lower edge divided into two squared feet so it can stand upright like a door taken off its hinges; the face is embossed with seven connected mountain ridges in high relief; the leather arm straps on the back are newer replacements. Bright white light leaks out along the ridgelines of the mountain pattern, one peak after another.

name: 余烬高灯
look: a small palm-sized hanging lantern with a tall slender copper frame and a ring for lifting it high; at the top two layers of outward-flaring copper eaves, shaped like a bird's folded wings; there is no oil and no wick inside: only a single grain of grey ash floating in the center of the open lamp body, giving off a warm orange-white light. Simple soldier smith's work, holding a divine ember.

name: 冬牙白裘
look: a long white fur coat that would reach past the knees, thick snowy hide whose fur roots shade to pale ice-blue; six semi-transparent ice spines rise along the shoulders like the back of a frost rhinoceros; the high collar is fastened with one curved white horn tip; the inside is lined with a patch of old, worn tent canvas. Specks of blue-white light glint in the fur like snow that has been drawn into it.

name: 铃尾长绳
look: a huge coil of long rope made of hemp and animal sinew, wound in heavy loops; small copper bells are tied along it at every arm's length, joined with neat travelling knots; the rope is pieced from many generations of strands of different colours, newer brown sections spliced to old ones, the oldest stretches worn pale and bleached almost white. A thin golden thread of light runs along the rope beside the real strands, glinting from bell to bell.
